issue.title: Internal memory symbols still use the legacy short/long tier names after the core/reference rename
issue.description: 121 internal identifiers in the memory and AMD packages still spell the memory tiers short/long, contradicting the core/reference vocabulary the rest of the codebase now uses.

task_type_fields.impact:
No user-facing behavior is wrong: epic sase-sq phase sase-sq.1 (c9ca0db5f) renamed the vocabulary at every surface an agent or user sees, and `short`/`long` remain accepted forever on read by design. The cost is maintenance legibility — every reader of the memory and AMD packages now has to hold two names for one concept, and new code has no unambiguous convention to copy.

This is a pure internal rename with no wire, frontmatter, or document-anchor component: do NOT touch the `type: short|long` parsing aliases, the `_CORE_SECTION_RE` / `_REFERENCE_SECTION_RE` legacy anchor alternatives, or the `short_notes` / `long_notes` template-context aliases, all of which must keep accepting the old spellings. Symvision will flag any public symbol renamed without updating its importers, so rename call sites in the same change.

Proposed by phase bead sase-sq.1 (note 5), which deliberately deferred it so the user-facing rename could land on its own, and routed here by the sase-sq land agent.
task_type_fields.repro: Run `grep -rn "short_memory\|long_memory\|LongMemory\|ShortMemory" src --include='*.py' | grep -v __pycache__ | wc -l` — 121 hits on HEAD 39bc4bc70. The load-bearing ones are `GeneratedLongMemoryNote` and `render_long_memory_sections` in src/sase/memory/notes.py, `inlined_short_memory_files` and `_is_short_memory_note` in src/sase/memory/inventory_reachability.py, `_short_memory_paths` / `collect_long_memory_entries` / `_AmdLongMemoryEntry` / `_normalize_long_memory_description_lines` in src/sase/amd/_agents_doc.py, and `validate_short_memory_structure` in src/sase/amd/inline_memory.py. `GeneratedShortMemoryNote` is also constructed by src/sase/main/init_memory/root_planning.py when it overlays a core web descriptor body.
